name: glossary-candidates
title: Glossary candidates
description: Single- and multi-word term candidates for a glossary: tagset-agnostic POS patterns (or stopword-bounded n-grams on untagged corpora), ranked by C-value termhood, filtered by frequency and range, enriched with dispersion, an example sentence, a definitional context and top collocates; optionally exported to a spreadsheet.

patterns.description: Token patterns (e.g. ['NOUN', 'ADJ NOUN', 'NOUN ADP NOUN']); default: a set for the corpus language word order.

min_length.description: Minimum words per term (2 = multi-word terms only).

export_path.description: Optional .xlsx/.tsv path for the final table.

interpretation: CVALUE ranks termhood: frequent candidates that are not just fragments of longer terms score higher (it uses log2(length+1), so single words are included). TEXTS_PCT and DP show whether a term is general to the corpus or tied to a few texts. EXAMPLE gives a usage sentence; DEFINITION is a heuristic definitional context (verify it); TOP_COLLOCATES help write the entry. Remove generic words that are frequent but not terms (e.g. 'experience', 'ability') - for domain specificity run glossary-contrastive with a general reference corpus. Propose a definition for each retained term grounded in the example/definition sentences and cite the file.
